summary: Private deploy: custom DNS forwarder and resolver order causing intermittent service discovery and TLS timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent failures resolving Redwood control-plane endpoints from model-serving hosts in their private deployment. Failures correlate with 0.5–2s DNS resolution delays and subsequent TLS handshake timeouts for model pull and control-plane registration.

Impact: Multiple model-serving agents intermittently fail to pull model shards and drop active gRPC streams. Customer reports service degradation across 10% of hosts; automated restarts recover but cause request errors and elevated tail latency.

Environment details: Private deployment (air-gapped variant) using a customer-managed DNS forwarder (dnsmasq) that conditionally forwards certain domains to an on-prem BIND cluster (for internal names) and otherwise forwards to a cloud resolver. Hosts run Ubuntu 22.04 with systemd-resolved enabled; the deployment uses host-level /etc/resolv.conf managed by local agent.

Observed: 1) Occasional DNS queries for control-plane.redwood-inference.customer.svc return NXDOMAIN or time out for ~1–2s, then subsequent query succeeds. 2) When DNS query delays exceed 900ms, control-plane TLS handshake fails (client timeout) and model pull requests retried and sometimes routed to fallback model variant.

Expected: Deterministic, sub-50ms DNS resolution to Redwood control-plane endpoints; no TLS handshake timeouts under normal network conditions.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy private agent on customer host with customer-provided dnsmasq and systemd-resolved in default config.
2) Configure dnsmasq to forward *.customer.svc -> on-prem BIND (10.10.0.5) and other domains -> 8.8.8.8.
3) Start agent and observe startup registration; run repeated dig + tcpdump against control-plane FQDN.
4) Observe intermittent NXDOMAIN/NOERROR with long TTL zero and delays of 500–2000ms.
5) Trigger a model pull from the agent and observe TLS handshake timeout and grpc client error in agent logs.

Notes: Issue reproduces within 10–20 minutes under customer's DNS load pattern. Repro rate increases when BIND is under load or when conditional forwarding table is large.

# systemd-resolved stub resolver configured; dnsmasq sits on 127.0.0.2 and forwards to on-prem when match
investigation:
Initial hypothesis: resolver order and conditional forwarding introduce a blocking synchronous forward to on-prem BIND causing tail-latency on DNS. Observed resolver race where systemd-resolved forwards first to local dnsmasq which tries conditional forwarding; when BIND is slow, the resolver waits instead of failing fast to alternate upstream.

What we ran:
- dig +trace against control-plane domain from host and a container: shows conditional forward to on-prem BIND with variable response times.
- strace on agent process DNS calls: agent uses getaddrinfo() which blocks on system resolv.conf -> observed ~1s blocking during BIND slowness.
- tcpdump at dnsmasq and on-prem BIND: when BIND thread pool is saturated, tcp retransmits observed.
- Reviewed dnsmasq config: conditional-forward with long timeout (default 5s) and no DNS-over-TCP fallback.

Partial findings:
- systemd-resolved stub + dnsmasq chaining causes upstream timeouts to be honored by application-level blocking calls.
- On several hosts, /etc/nsswitch.conf lookup order had 'hosts: files dns', but libc resolver uses DNS stub which is synchronous.
- BIND cluster had occasional thread contention and one nameserver out-of-rotation during the incident window.

Cross-references: Slack thread #support-data-bridge (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C09SDFX12), Confluence runbook draft for private DNS (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Private+DNS+Recommendations), and related internal ticket INT-4128 investigating BIND capacity on customer's side.
comments: Customer (Raj Patel) - 2026-03-10: We're seeing roughly 8–12% of model pulls fail intermittently across our fleet during peak hours; this aligns with on-prem jobs we run that saturate our BIND. Can Redwood recommend a short-term mitigation?
Support (Aisha Malik) - 2026-03-10: Thanks Raj — investigating. Can you provide tcpdump from an affected host and dnsmasq config? Also confirm whether you run DNS-over-TCP for large responses.

Customer (Raj Patel) - 2026-03-10: Uploaded tcpdump and dnsmasq.conf to the ticket; no DNS-over-TCP configured. BIND is a 3-node cluster with two nodes behind HA proxy. We can increase thread pool but want a safer mitigation first.

SRE (Diego Rivas) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with a test BIND that sleeps on queries. Short-term mitigation: set dnsmasq 'timeout' lower (e.g., 500ms) and enable 'resolv-file' with a hard-coded control-plane A records for agent bootstrap. Also recommend enabling TCP fallback and decreasing glibc resolver retry. Will prepare a patch to agent to add DNS caching & host override support.

Customer (Raj Patel) - 2026-03-11: Applied dnsmasq timeout=500 and added static A entries for control-plane IPs; issue incidence dropped to <0.5% within 30 minutes. We will provision more BIND capacity as a long-term fix.

Support (Aisha Malik) - 2026-03-12: Verified customer mitigation. Scheduling follow-up to add guidance to the private-deploy runbook and agent change to surface DNS latency metrics. Marking ticket In Progress while we track agent patch rollout.
resolution:
Workaround applied: customer lowered dnsmasq upstream timeout, added static host overrides for control-plane bootstrap, and enabled DNS-over-TCP fallback. These changes reduced incidents immediately.

Permanent fix / follow-up:
1) Engineering to add DNS latency telemetry and host-override mechanism in agent (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/agent/pull/2276).
2) Update private deployment runbook with recommended DNS config: prefer low upstream timeouts, enable TCP fallback, avoid large conditional-forward tables on critical path, and provide sample dnsmasq/resolved configs.
3) Customer to scale BIND worker pool; SRE to validate.

Ticket status: waiting on agent PR rollout and runbook update; set to Resolved after patch verification.
